verdict.rationale: Paxos documents registrable webhook endpoints that receive asynchronous platform events. Each webhook is configured with event types and API Key or OAuth endpoint auth, with 24-hour retries and a List Events API for recovering failed deliveries. Orchestration webhooks fire on status transitions for mint/redeem (conversion plus transfer/withdrawal) flows, so state can be tracked without polling. However, payload signing is not evidenced; auth is API key/OAuth to your endpoint rather than signed payloads. Specific payment-confirmed, payout-settled and conversion-executed event types are not enumerated. Missing for 10: documented payload signature verification, an explicit catalog of payment/payout/conversion event types, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, money movement emits signed webhooks — payment confirmed, payout settled, conversion executed — so my system tracks state without polling chains or dashboards

citations.quote: Paxos Webhooks allow you to register your own endpoints to receive asynchronous events driven by the Paxos Platform.
Secure the endpoint using either API key or OAuth-based authentication.
There are two families of orchestration webhook events: a high-level family that fires once per top-level status transition, and a granular family that fires at each sub-state change.
Paxos will continue retry attempts for up to **24 hours** from the initial attempt, unless delivery succeeds.
